title: JB Financial Accounting: middle school career day presentation on accounting careers, designations and professional organizations
participant_role: Staff accountant at JB Financial Accounting preparing a career day presentation
judge_role: Accounting supervisor at JB Financial Accounting reviewing the presentation before career day
scenario:
You are to assume the role of an accountant at JB FINANCIAL ACCOUNTING. A local middle school asked the company to participate in their annual career day and your supervisor (judge) has asked you to prepare a presentation about career opportunities in accounting.

Your supervisor (judge) wants you to represent JB FINANCIAL ACCOUNTING and present information about careers in accounting to 200 middle school students. There will be four other speakers in other fields also presenting career information, so your presentation must be kept under 10 minutes.

The presentation must be geared toward middle school students and focus on:
- Various career opportunities in accounting
- The roles and responsibilities of accounting professionals
- Career-advancement activities and resources within the industry

The students have already submitted a few general questions they want each speaker to provide answers regarding their industries. The student questions include:
- Are there any opportunities for travel in your industry?
- Does a career in your industry provide a stable income?
- Are technology skills needed in your industry?

You will give your presentation to your supervisor (judge) in a role-play to take place in the supervisor's (judge's) office in preparation for the career day. The supervisor (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your presentation. After you have given the presentation and have answered the supervisor's (judge's) questions, the supervisor (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
tasks: The roles and responsibilities of accounting professionals
Career-advancement activities and resources within the industry

Answer the students' submitted questions: Are there any opportunities for travel in your industry? Does a career in your industry provide a stable income? Are technology skills needed in your industry?

solution.overview: A strong answer is a short, lively career talk for 12 to 14 year olds: it introduces three or more accounting careers (for example forensic accountant, management accountant and tax advisor), explains what each does day to day, covers the designations (CPA, CMA, CFE, EA) and professional organizations (AICPA, IMA) that help accountants advance, stresses that accountants keep learning throughout their careers, and answers the students' three questions about travel, income stability and technology.

answer: Forensic accountant: a financial detective who investigates embezzlement, fraud and money laundering and may testify in court
Management accountant: works inside a company analyzing data, preparing budgets and evaluating projects to guide managers; can advance to CFO
Tax advisor: helps people and businesses follow tax laws while paying no more than they must; prepares returns and plans tax strategies
Other paths to mention briefly: auditor, government accountant, bookkeeper, sports or entertainment business manager

by_task.task: Roles and responsibilities of accounting professionals
answer: Record and organize a business's financial transactions accurately and honestly
Prepare financial statements and tax returns that others rely on, following GAAP and tax law
Analyze the numbers to help owners and managers make decisions
Protect the public: accountants must act ethically, keep information confidential and report fraud

Designations: CPA (Certified Public Accountant), CMA (Certified Management Accountant), CFE (Certified Fraud Examiner), EA (Enrolled Agent); each requires education, an exam and experience and boosts pay and opportunities
Professional organizations such as the AICPA and the IMA offer networking, job boards, publications and continuing education
Ongoing education is required: CPAs must complete continuing professional education hours every year because tax laws, accounting standards and technology keep changing
Internships, college accounting degrees and student clubs (DECA, FBLA) are the first steps
Travel: yes for some roles, forensic accountants travel to gather evidence or testify, auditors visit client sites; management accountants and tax advisors travel little
Stable income: yes, every business and person needs accounting and tax help, so demand is steady; tax season adds extra earning potential and management accountants can rise to CFO
Technology: yes, accountants use Excel, financial modeling software, tax software and data analysis and fraud detection tools; forensic accounting needs the most advanced tech skills

judge_question_answers.question: Which career opportunity do you think the students will find most exciting?
answer: Forensic accounting: it is like being a detective, uncovering fraud and money laundering and sometimes testifying in court
It combines puzzles, technology and real consequences, which appeals to middle schoolers who enjoy mysteries and crime shows
Pair it with a relatable example, such as how forensic accountants helped catch a famous fraud

judge_question_answers.question: What advice can you give them for high school that will help them with a future career in accounting?
answer: Take math, business, accounting and computer courses, and get comfortable with spreadsheets
Join DECA or FBLA and compete in finance events to practice presenting and problem solving
Look for part-time jobs or volunteer roles that involve handling money, such as treasurer of a club
Practice communication skills; accountants must explain numbers clearly to non-accountants

key_concepts.definition: An accountant who investigates financial crimes such as fraud, embezzlement and money laundering, analyzes records for irregularities and may give expert testimony in court.
An accountant who works inside a company preparing budgets, analyzing costs and evaluating projects to help managers make decisions.
An accountant who prepares tax returns and plans tax strategies so clients comply with tax law while legally minimizing what they owe.
The most recognized accounting license; requires a college degree, passing the CPA exam and work experience, and allows the holder to sign audit reports.
A credential from the IMA for accountants who specialize in internal business analysis, budgeting and strategy.
A designation for professionals who detect and investigate fraud.
A federally licensed tax practitioner authorized to represent taxpayers before the IRS.
The American Institute of CPAs, the national professional organization for CPAs that sets standards, offers continuing education and provides networking and career resources.
The professional organization for management accountants that awards the CMA and provides education, research and networking.
Ongoing training hours licensed accountants must complete each year to keep up with changing laws, standards and technology.
A credential earned through education, an exam and experience that proves expertise and raises earning potential and job opportunities.
Adjusting vocabulary, examples and length to the listeners, here middle school students in under 10 minutes.

notes: The PDF SOLUTION says solutions will vary and gives three example careers (forensic accountant, management accountant, tax advisor) with roles, technology, travel, education and stability, plus a paragraph on designations and organizations. Judge question answers are model answers. No numeric data or tables in this role-play.
